item.title: APC youths united under Dayo Israel, Obidike says
item.description: A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Chief Obidike Chukwuebuka, has dismissed reports of disunity within the party’s youth wing, insisting that it remains united under the leadership of its National Youth Leader, Hon. Dayo Israel. Obidike, a former aspirant for the position of APC National Youth Leader, spoke in Abuja on Tuesday after a strategic meeting of party youth stakeholders. He attributed reports of divisions within the youth wing to individuals uncomfortable with what he described as the unity and renewed mobilisation under Israel’s leadership. “As someone who contested for the same office and who understands the dynamics of the youth wing, I can tell you authoritatively that there is no crisis. “What we have today is a united, re-energised and focused APC Youth Wing. Hon. Dayo Israel has shown uncommon leadership, maturity and inclusiveness. He has carried everyone along, including those of us who contested against him. That is the hallmark of a true leader,” Obidike said. He said the youth wing had evolved from a party organ into a strategic electoral structure, with a presence across the country and in tertiary institutions. According to him, APC youths are now focused on mobilising support for President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general elections rather than engaging in internal disputes. “Our eyes are on the ball. Our principal, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, has shown courageous leadership in repositioning Nigeria. It is now the duty of we the youths to reward him with massive support. “I want to assure Mr President that Nigerian youths under the leadership of Hon. Dayo Israel are ready, mobilised, and will deliver no less than 15 million youth votes to secure his re-election in January 2027,” he said. Obidike urged APC youths across the six geopolitical zones to disregard reports of disaffection and continue to support Israel and the party’s leadership. “We are one family. The old politics of division is over. Dayo Israel is our leader and we are solidly behind him. Together, we will make history in 2027,” he added. The post APC youths united under Dayo Israel, Obidike says appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Atiku will lose polling unit to Tinubu, APC declares
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Deputy National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Ali Bukar Dalori, has predicted that former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar will lose even his polling unit in Adamawa State to President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. Atiku, who is the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), hails from Adamawa State. Dalori, who spoke on Wednesday in Abuja at the graduation ceremony of women trained under the Tinubu-Shettima Village-to-Village campaign, also predicted that Tinubu would defeat Atiku in Borno, Yobe and other states in the North-East. “I don’t think that Atiku can disrupt the North-East. Why? Even Adamawa, his hometown, he will not win, even at his polling unit. I will assure you of that,” he said. Dalori said his prediction was informed by his experience as a grassroots politician and his understanding of the region’s political dynamics. He cited ongoing federal road projects as a major factor he believes would boost the APC’s chances in the region. The projects, he said, included the Gombe-Bauchi and Bauchi-Maiduguri roads, as well as the Maiduguri-Gamboru Ngala corridor linking Nigeria with Chad. He also referred to sections of the Maiduguri-Biu road that had previously been left incomplete, arguing that the continuation of such projects could strengthen the ruling party’s appeal to voters. Dalori said residents would consider the projects when deciding whom to support in 2027, adding that the contest should not be judged solely on Atiku’s place of origin or past electoral performance. In the 2023 presidential election, Atiku, then the candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), won Adamawa and other states in the North-East, while Tinubu secured the presidency despite losing several northern states to opposition parties. Dalori also defended the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms, particularly the removal of the petrol subsidy and changes to the foreign exchange regime, describing them as necessary measures to stabilise public finances and reposition the economy. He acknowledged that the reforms had generated debate and concerns over the cost of living but argued that they should be assessed alongside the administration’s infrastructure projects and other development initiatives. The APC chieftain also cited Vice-President Kashim Shettima’s origin as a factor he believes could strengthen the party’s prospects in the North-East. “Shettima is from Borno, from the North-East. He is our son. Because of that, we can do everything to ensure that Tinubu comes back for a second term,” Dalori said. Meanwhile, National Coordinator of the Tinubu-Shettima Village-to-Village campaign, Ambassador Farida Musa Jauro, pledged to mobilise more than one million votes for Tinubu across northern Nigeria through grassroots engagement and political sensitisation. item.title: Ebola: No gathering restrictions advised for Nigeria – WHO
item.description: By Dickson Omobola The World Health Organisation (WHO), Wednesday, said it had not advised the Federal Government to restrict public gatherings following the Ebola case recorded in the country. The organisation, however, said Nigeria would need to go 42 days without another Ebola case to be declared Ebola-free, while 53 people who had contact with the patient remained under surveillance. Speaking on Arise TV, Executive Director of the WHO Health Emergencies Programme, Dr Chikwe Ihekweazu, clarified that the patient’s medical evacuation was carried out at the request of her country of origin and was not due to any shortcomings in Nigeria’s capacity to manage the case. Ihekweazu also commended Nigeria’s response to the case, saying the speed of laboratory confirmation and sequencing, as well as the measures taken by the government to contain the outbreak, were commendable. He said, “We have advised the country to have appropriate response measures to this, and they have carried this out more or less to the letter. We have had excellent case management in Nigeria. Lab confirmation happened very quickly. We had the sequence happen very quickly. I think appropriate measures have been carried out. Nigerians can be proud of the response so far. We have not advised any restriction of further gatherings. Our advice is never political; it is always technical, and we will continue to support government in this response. “The key thing now is for every single contact that the patient had to be followed up with every single day, as is happening, to ensure that there is no further transmission. If there is transmission, it must be detected early and responded to appropriately. So, for now, I think the key thing is to keep this as a technical response, trust the government, and trust these agencies. They are being supported by the World Health Organisation in all ramifications of the response, and I am confident that we can support government to get this under control and not politicise this event at all.” In the period required for Nigeria to be declared Ebola-free, he said, “For certain diseases, a group of diseases we call the viral haemorrhagic fevers, of which Ebola is one of them, we consider every single case equivalent to an outbreak and requiring a coordinated response. In this case, that is exactly why we raised the alarm and supported the government to do what it needed to do to respond. Yesterday, we saw the medical evacuation on the request of the country from which the patient came. This wasn’t as a response to any deficit in the management capacities in Nigeria. item.title: Workers protest at coastal highway site in Cross River
item.description: By Emma Una CALABAR — About 600 workers at Section 3B of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway project in Cross River State have protested over alleged poor working conditions, salary cuts, intimidation and the demand for the reinstatement of the state liaison officer. The protest, which began on October 26, continued on Wednesday at the Hitech Construction Yard in Awi, Akamkpa Local Government Area, about 30 kilometres from Calabar, where the section of the highway project begins. The workers, carrying placards, accused the project management of unfair treatment and alleged that newly arrived Lebanese expatriates had refused to work with the Cross River State Liaison Officer, Mr Asuquo Ukpayang, and brought in a Community Liaison Officer they could control. The protesters said their action was aimed at securing better working conditions, protecting their welfare and ensuring fair treatment of Nigerian workers. A large crowd gathered in front of the construction yard, while some military personnel observed the protest. Speaking with journalists, Esikere Peter, a quality control and laboratory worker, alleged that the number of hours recognised for payment had been reduced from eight to two, resulting in significant salary losses. Peter also claimed that night shifts had been removed from workers’ payment records despite some employees working until 11 p.m. “We, the workers of this project, are not protesting to destroy property or cause violence. We just want the Nigerian workers to be treated fairly and with dignity,” he said. Similarly, Stephen Oke, a trailer driver, accused the expatriates of intimidating Nigerian workers and treating them disrespectfully, urging the company’s management to address their complaints. Oke alleged that Nigerian labourers performed much of the work under harsh conditions but were cheated, mistreated, short-changed and underpaid. He also accused the project manager, identified as Mr Boutrous, of arbitrary dismissals, intimidation and threats against workers. According to him, some employees were penalised for requesting materials needed to perform their duties. The protesters demanded the removal of the project manager, the site manager, identified as Mr Tony, and the earth-moving supervisor, Mr Shabel, whom they accused of treating workers unfairly. Another protester, Mr Ana Matthew, an earth-moving and level-checking worker, alleged that employees worked under harsh weather conditions without adequate shelter. Matthew also accused the management of using military personnel to intimidate workers and claimed that their payments had been reduced despite working during the day and at night. He further alleged that scrap materials previously shared among employees had been sold without their consent. The workers called for the return of personnel familiar with the project’s foundation, saying they supported the coastal highway because of its potential to improve road connectivity across the Niger Delta. item.title: Rep calls for extension of JAMB admission deadline for public, private varsities
item.description: …Says short timeline could deny qualified candidates access to higher education By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Basic Education, Hon. Oboku Oforji, has appealed to the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) to extend the deadline for the completion of admissions into public and private universities for the 2026/2027 academic session. Oforji made the appeal in Abuja on Wednesday while addressing journalists at the National Assembly, expressing concern that the tight admission schedule could disadvantage many candidates seeking placement in universities and other tertiary institutions across the country. The lawmaker argued that extending the deadline would provide prospective students with a fairer opportunity to secure admission, particularly those who have demonstrated a strong desire to pursue higher education despite the various challenges confronting them. He stressed that the admission process should take into account the circumstances of candidates and ensure that qualified students are not unnecessarily denied opportunities to further their education because of time constraints. According to him, JAMB should demonstrate flexibility by allowing institutions and prospective students additional time to complete the necessary admission procedures. “It is important that JAMB extend the deadline for the admission of our children across the country. I think it is very important that I appeal to the leadership of JAMB. We have also formally reached out to them to appeal to them, and I believe we are together in this journey for the betterment of education in our country. “I am particularly happy with the commitment of the children and their level of willingness to go to school. In recognition of this commitment, I think it is important for JAMB to immediately extend the deadline for the admission of our children across the country,” Oforji said. The lawmaker maintained that providing prospective students with adequate time to complete the admission process would support the country’s broader educational objectives and help ensure that more qualified candidates gain access to tertiary education. He also called for continued cooperation between JAMB, tertiary institutions and other relevant stakeholders to address challenges associated with the admission process and safeguard the educational aspirations of Nigerian youths. The appeal comes against the backdrop of JAMB’s recently announced deadlines for the completion of admissions into tertiary institutions for the 2026/2027 academic session. The examination body had, in a statement issued on Monday, directed public universities to conclude their admission processes on or before October 31, 2026, while private universities are expected to complete theirs by November 30, 2026. item.title: [UPDATED] High-Speed Train Collision In Spain Kills 64, Injures Over 100
item.description: A high-speed train collision south of Madrid in Spain killed 64 people and injured scores more on Wednesday, with the toll likely to rise, authorities said in one of Europe’s deadliest such disasters this century. One train on the scene in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha was seen embedded into another after the second such accident to strike Spain this year. This still image from video taken and released by Spain’s Civil Guard on October 28, 2026 shows an aerial scene of a train crash between a high-speed Renfe AVE train and an Iryo train around 150 km south of Madrid between Urda and Los Yebenes in the province of Toledo. (Photo by Handout / Guardia Civil / AFP) Some carriages were lying on their side in tangles of metal debris at the bottom of an embankment, while dozens of emergency services vehicles were racing to and from the site. “We are speaking of approximately 64 (dead), but this is probably going to grow even more,” Castilla-La Mancha’s leader Emiliano Garcia-Page told reporters at the scene, raising a previous toll of 31. A spokeswoman from the Castilla-La Mancha government said that more than 100 people had been injured. Of them, 58 had been taken to hospital, with 15 in a critical condition. Helicopters hovered above the site during a frantic search for survivors, while several black vans arrived from a funeral parlour. State railway operator Renfe confirmed in a statement that the main high-speed line from Madrid to southern Spain had been suspended after one of its services suffered an accident with a train from private Spanish company Iryo. Iryo said in a statement that its train, which was carrying 147 passengers and five staff, including the driver, “was hit from behind” by the Renfe service. This still image from video taken and released by Spain’s Emergency Military Unit (UME) on October 28, 2026 shows military rescue personnel working at the scene of a train crash between a high-speed Renfe AVE train and an Iryo train around 150 km south of Madrid between Urda and Los Yebenes in the province of Toledo. Photo by HANDOUT / UME / AFP A visibly shaken Manuel Ortiz, 49, who lives in the nearby village of Urda, around 130 kilometres (80 miles) south of Madrid, told AFP he had been transporting survivors all morning in his car. Ortiz added that the passengers of the Iryo told him their train was stationary when the collision happened, describing a “horrific, horrible” scene that “smelled of an accident, of metal”. Rail Safety Under Scrutiny The accident comes one month before Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who faced heavy criticism for this year’s first disaster, seeks to overturn unfavourable polls and extend his eight-year premiership in an early general election on November 29. item.title: Yoruba Group demands Oduduwa Republic, restrictions on non-indigenes
item.description: By Adeola Badru IBADAN — The Yoruba Self Determination Movement (YSDM) has renewed its call for an independent Oduduwa Republic, proposing restrictions on non-indigenes’ political participation, land ownership and access to commercial spaces in parts of the South-West. The group made the demands on Wednesday at a press conference organised by the Yoruba Action Group at the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) Press Centre, Iyaganku, Ibadan. Its Deputy Leader (Homeland), Architect George Akinola, said Nigeria’s worsening security challenges, political tensions and disagreements over ethnic identity and territorial ownership had strengthened the movement’s position that the country should be dissolved rather than restructured. Akinola said the group had warned between 2017 and 2022 that Nigeria was “tottering on the brink of disaster”, arguing that restructuring, resource control and a return to regionalism would not resolve the country’s fundamental problems. “We added, among other things, that it is too late for restructuring, resource control or regionalism in Nigeria,” he said. He maintained that an independent Oduduwa Republic remained the movement’s preferred solution to what he described as threats to Yoruba political, economic and cultural interests. The group’s proposals also included restrictions on non-indigenes’ participation in markets, land leases and elections, as well as tighter migration controls in Yoruba urban centres. Akinola accused armed groups operating in parts of the South-West of kidnapping, killing and attacking farmers and other residents. He also alleged that disputes over commercial activities and claims concerning the historical ownership of Lagos had heightened tensions between Yoruba and Igbo communities. “The Yoruba people are angry and fed up with Nigeria. What we desire most, at this time, is to become a sovereign nation, separate from dysfunctional Nigeria and its many encumbrances on Yoruba potential,” he said. Seeks restrictions on political participation The movement rejected claims that Lagos was “No Man’s Land” or that Igbo residents had played a decisive role in developing the state, insisting that Lagos was historically and culturally part of Yorubaland. It identified the Awori, Ijebu, Egba, Egbado, Remo, Ilaje and Egun communities, alongside Yoruba returnees from Sierra Leone, as populations associated with the historical development of Lagos. Citing historical accounts attributed to Sola Ebiseni, the group argued that Yoruba lineages had shaped Lagos’ traditional institutions, including the succession of its monarchs and the composition of prominent royal families. It also disputed claims of historical Bini sovereignty over Lagos, arguing that the traditional succession system on Lagos Island reflected Yoruba ruling-house arrangements. item.title: Tinubu has done more for Plateau than past presidents — Yilwatda
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, has said President Bola Tinubu has done more for Plateau State than previous Nigerian presidents, citing projects and interventions by the current administration. Yilwatda spoke on Wednesday at the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement rally in Jos, where he urged APC supporters to back Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, arguing that Plateau had no reason to support another presidential candidate. “Your son is the national chairman of the APC. We are part and parcel of the system. We are in the inner caucus of the system. We have no reason to thumbprint any other presidential candidate on the Plateau at all,” he said. “President Bola Tinubu is a friend of Plateau State. No president in the history of Nigeria has been able to stand with the state the way Mr President has done for us,” Yilwatda added. The APC chairman also criticised former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, questioning the projects executed in Plateau during his eight years in office. “Atiku Abubakar, the presidential candidate of the ADC, was vice-president for eight years. Show me one road or one thing that we had on the Plateau. Show me one N10 billion project on the Plateau within that period,” he said. Yilwatda said previous administrations had offered the state relatively small interventions, citing boreholes and tricycles, popularly known as Keke NAPEP, in contrast with what he described as major projects being attracted by the Tinubu administration. “The best we could have in those days was a borehole, or they would bring Keke Napep for us. Today, the President is bringing major projects to the Plateau,” he said. He added that Tinubu had provided a university and assigned several projects to the state, citing investments in education, healthcare, infrastructure and security. On insecurity, Yilwatda said it remained Plateau’s foremost challenge but claimed the President had taken steps to address it. “If you ask any Plateau man, ‘What is your problem?’ The number one problem is insecurity, and Mr President has addressed it,” he said. Also speaking at the rally, Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang declared his support for Tinubu, saying a meeting with the President on June 6, 2023, had convinced him of Tinubu’s commitment to Nigeria, despite their political differences at the time. “Let me make a public confession for the first time: when I met with the President sometime on June 6, 2023, I made up my mind that this was the president to travel with,” Mutfwang said. The governor acknowledged that the country continued to face challenges but expressed confidence in the administration’s direction, particularly on security. “Yes, we are not there yet. item.title: YPP urges NASS to suspend Tinubu’s $20.5bn loan
item.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja The presidential candidate of the Young Progressives Party (YPP), Architect Peter Agada, has urged the National Assembly to suspend consideration of President Bola Tinubu’s latest external borrowing request until after the 2027 general elections. Agada made the call in Abuja on Wednesday in reaction to Tinubu’s letter to Senate President Godswill Akpabio seeking approval for $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion in supplementary external borrowing for 2026 and 2027. He said the timing of the request, less than 110 days before the elections, raised concerns, particularly with Nigeria’s public debt standing at ₦166.79 trillion as of June 2026. “Now we want to add another $21.7bn — less than 110 days to the 2027 general election. “For three years, the Federal Government has been unable to fully finance its budget. Capital performance is below 40 per cent. “Contractors are being owed. Yet we are borrowing more. In architecture, you don’t borrow to build a new house when you have not roofed the old one,” he said. The YPP candidate questioned why the government continued to seek substantial loans despite the removal of the petrol subsidy and the floating of the naira, which he said had significantly increased government revenue. “Where did the subsidy savings go? This is the question Emir Sanusi and other leaders have been asking,” he said. Agada also questioned what tangible results the proposed borrowing could deliver within the remaining period before the elections, given the time required to implement major infrastructure projects. “If you approve $20.5bn today, can you complete any power, transport, health or education project in 100 days? No. So what will this money actually do? Pay contractors who are party financiers? Fund election logistics?” he asked. He urged lawmakers to include a clause prohibiting disbursement of the loan proceeds between January and May 2027 if the request was approved. “If you must approve this loan, insert a clear clause: No disbursement from January 2027 to May 2027. The money should come after the election, to whoever wins, not before to the incumbent. That is how you prove it is not political,” he said. Agada argued that the borrowing request could send conflicting signals to investors, given the government’s promotion of its economic reforms and reported endorsements from international development institutions. He proposed alternative ways of financing infrastructure without resorting to additional borrowing, claiming that Nigeria could save more than ₦13 trillion annually through leaner governance without reducing Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) distributions or introducing new taxes. His proposals included cutting the cost of governance by 40 per cent, merging 250 agencies he described as duplicative into 40, and eliminating duplicate vehicle fleets and official trips, which he said could save more than ₦4 trillion. item.title: ‘I can take bullet for him’ — Uba Sani vows to support Tinubu till last minute
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, has declared his readiness to defend President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, saying he can take a bullet for the President and will support him until the last minute. Sani said his support was informed by the benefits Kaduna State had received under the Tinubu administration, including federal appointments, infrastructure projects and funding for transportation and education. Speaking in an interview with Trust TV’s Daily Politics , the governor said his loyalty to Tinubu was driven by the interests of Kaduna State rather than personal favours. Asked whether he could take a political bullet for Tinubu, Sani replied, “I can take it.” He added: “I have no apology for supporting President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and I will continue to support him till last minute and I will tell you why, because many people do not know President Tinubu, I know him, and I’ve been with him for 32 years and I cannot pretend.” According to the governor, Tinubu’s support had helped Kaduna secure key federal appointments and major development projects. Sani cited the appointment of three Kaduna indigenes to strategic federal positions: Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (retd.); Minister of Environment, Balarabe Abbas Lawal; and Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Shehu Dikko. He said he had engaged the President on the appointments, which he described as important to the state’s representation in the Federal Government. “The minister of defence is from Kaduna, Christopher Musa, and I was instrumental in getting him the portfolio. The minister of environment, Balarabe Abbas, is from Kaduna, and recently, when the ministry of sports was collapsed into the national sports commission, Shehu Dikko is from Kaduna,” he said. “Now we have three ministers, and I was instrumental in talking to Mr President. What do I need more than this?” On education, Sani said he had initially requested two additional federal universities for Kaduna, but Tinubu approved four university initiatives. They include the Federal University of Applied Sciences in Kachia, the Federal University of Education in Zaria, the Umaru Musa Yar’Adua University of Petroleum Resources in Rigachikun, and a proposed conversion of Kaduna Polytechnic into a federal university of technology. The governor also credited Tinubu with facilitating funding for the 123-kilometre Kaduna-Birnin Gwari road, which he said had been abandoned for 45 years. He said the President had promised to reconstruct the road during a campaign visit to Kaduna in 2022. Sani said he later reminded Tinubu of the pledge by showing him a video of the commitment, after which N178 billion was released for the project. He added that funding had also been approved for the reconstruction of the road linking Jama’a, Kwoi and Jere, which he said had been in poor condition for nearly four decades. item.title: Barau faults Osinbajo’s gloomy assessment of Nigeria’s economy, democracy
item.description: By Henry Umoru, Abuja The Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, APC, Kano North has taken a swipe at former Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo over the gloomy picture he painted of Nigeria’s economy and democratic governance. Senator Barau Jibrin, who noted that Osinbajo got it wrong, said that the administration of President Bola Tinubu is taking steps to address what he described as longstanding challenges confronting the country. According to Jibrin, while Osinbajo’s concerns, particularly those drawn from Afrobarometer surveys on Nigeria and other African countries, were valid, the government needs to improve communication with the people to highlight ongoing efforts to address the challenges. The Deputy President of the Senate made the remarks in Yola, Adamawa State, during a public lecture titled “Democracy and Development: Rethinking the Leadership Question,” organised to commemorate the 59th birthday of Adamawa State Governor, Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri. Osinbajo, who served as vice-president under former President Muhammadu Buhari from 2015 to 2023, expressed concern in his lecture about the failure of democratic governance among citizens across Africa after almost three decades of uninterrupted democratic rule in several countries. Citing Afrobarometer surveys, the former vice-president, who was defeated by President Tinubu during the APC presidential primary ahead of the 2023 general elections, highlighted widespread dissatisfaction with democratic institutions, economic hardship, declining public confidence in government and diminishing youth participation in electoral politics. He noted that although 64 per cent of Africans preferred democracy to other forms of government, only 38 per cent were satisfied with the way democracy was working in their respective countries. Osinbajo also cited findings indicating that 59 per cent of Africans considered their national economies to be in bad shape, while 51 per cent said their economies had deteriorated. He further expressed concern over the rising cost of living, unemployment, inadequate access to healthcare and declining voter turnout, warning that persistent hardship could weaken public confidence in democracy, particularly among young people. In a statement from his Media Office on Wednesday, Jibrin, while responding to the presentation, described Osinbajo’s lecture as thought-provoking and intellectually stimulating but said the gloomy picture painted by the surveys was being addressed and that the gaps were partly attributable to inadequate communication between governments and citizens. item.title: Russia woos African leaders at Moscow summit
item.description: A summit with nearly two dozen African leaders opened in Moscow Wednesday, with the Kremlin describing their countries as “natural allies” against the West. The two-day Russia-Africa summit, the third since 2019, comes as Moscow grapples with heavy Western sanctions over its Ukraine offensive and as it provides security assistance to several African governments. Moscow has courted ties with Africa since the Soviet era, and has long looked to the continent as a counterweight to what it sees as Western domination over international affairs. “We are natural allies in building a multipolar world order,” Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said of the summit, referring to a system where political power is no longer concentrated in the West. Russian President Vladimir Putin meanwhile said that that multipolar world was quickly becoming a reality, in an “irreversible” trend. “The era when the fate of entire continents was determined by a narrow bloc of states is irrevocably gone,” he said as he opened a Russia-Africa economic forum, which gathered thousands of Russian and African business leaders in Moscow hours before the high-level summit began. He told the delegations from 48 African countries, including 22 represented by their leaders, that Russia was “prepared to further expand the geographical reach of our agricultural product shipments”. The pledge came as attacks in the Black Sea linked to the conflict in Ukraine continue to disrupt exports of grain from both Russia and Ukraine. – ‘Neocolonialism’ – Putin also announced that Moscow planned to “localise” the production of “effective Russian medicines and vaccines” on the African continent, and noted that the number of African students in Russia had swelled 50 percent since 2020. The Russian president also stressed that his country was “open to sharing our modern competencies and high-tech digital know-how with our African friends”. Putin’s criticism of what he calls Western “neocolonialism” in Africa has resonated on the continent. That is especially true in the Sahel, where Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso have turned their backs on their former colonial ruler France in favour of closer ties with Moscow. Among the around 20 bilateral meetings Putin was scheduled to have with African leaders in Moscow this week was one with his Malian counterpart Assimi Goita, whose government is using Russian paramilitaries to battle a jihadist offensive. – DRC-Rwanda tensions – Putin was also due to meet with Democratic Republic of Congo President Felix Tshisekedi, who is attending the summit as tensions between his country and neighbouring Rwanda continue to flare. The Rwandan-backed M23 movement has seized swathes of the eastern DRC since taking up arms again in 2021, and, despite a US-brokered truce last December, fighting has continued. item.title: Reps approve ₦100.5bn reimbursement for Yobe airport
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has approved a ₦100.5 billion promissory note programme to reimburse the Yobe State Government for constructing the Muhammadu Buhari International Cargo Airport in Damaturu. The approved amount is ₦100,509,017,234.55, following the Federal Government’s decision to take over the newly constructed airport. The approval followed consideration of a report by the House Committee on Aids, Loans and Debt Management on Wednesday. Chairman of the committee, Abubakar Hassan Nalaraba, said during a briefing with journalists at the National Assembly, Abuja, that the committee conducted due diligence and inspected the facility before recommending the reimbursement. He said officials of the Federal Ministries of Aviation and Finance, alongside other relevant agencies, provided technical assessments and documentation on the project. “After due diligence and considerations, and after undertaking comprehensive oversight of the airport, receiving the reports of technical officials at the Ministry of Aviation, Ministry of Finance and the accounting office, we recently considered and approved the reimbursement of the airport to Yobe State Government,” Nalaraba said. He added that the committee found the quality of the airport’s infrastructure and equipment satisfactory, noting that professionals had certified the facilities as meeting the required standards. The committee’s report stated that the Federal Ministry of Aviation inspected the completed airport and confirmed that the quality of work met the standards required for its takeover by the Federal Government. It also found that the Yobe State Government had paid the contractors who executed the project, while the Bureau of Public Procurement certified that due process was followed. According to the report, the committee examined submissions from the state government, the Federal Ministries of Finance and Aviation, the Federal Executive Council and the Bureau of Public Procurement. It also reviewed contract agreements, certificates of completion, evidence of payments to contractors, due-process reviews and the bureau’s certificate of no objection. President Bola Tinubu had requested the National Assembly’s approval for the promissory note programme in a communication read on the floor of the House on October 13, 2026. The request was made pursuant to the Debt Management Office (Establishment) Act, 2003, and the Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2007, which provide for legislative approval of the programme. Promissory note programmes are used to settle outstanding Federal Government liabilities, including reimbursements to state governments for projects executed on behalf of the Federal Government. item.title: NNPCL to resume oil exploration in Borno
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) has pledged to resume oil exploration activities in Borno State, while assuring the state government of steps to address delays in upgrading the Maiduguri Emergency Power Plant. The commitments were made on Wednesday when Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, received the NNPCL management team, led by the board chairman, Engr. Ahmadu Musa Kida, in Maiduguri. The meeting focused on energy development, the resumption of oil exploration in the state and the delayed completion of the emergency power plant upgrade. Zulum stressed the strategic importance of resuming exploration in the Borno Basin, noting that the state had considerable commercial potential and shared borders with three countries. He expressed optimism that renewed exploration efforts by the national oil company would help unlock the state’s hydrocarbon resources and stimulate economic development. The governor, however, expressed concern over the slow pace of work on the Maiduguri Emergency Power Plant, describing the facility as critical to improving electricity supply in the state. He said the materials required for the plant’s upgrade had been on site for about two years, yet the project remained incomplete. Zulum urged the NNPCL management to intervene and remove the bottlenecks delaying the project, stressing that its completion was important to the socio-economic well-being of residents of Maiduguri and neighbouring communities. Responding, Kida assured the governor of the company’s readiness to fast-track the resumption of exploration activities in the Borno Basin and address the challenges delaying the power plant upgrade. He also commended Zulum for his continued support and efforts to create a conducive environment for investment in the state. The meeting was attended by the Deputy Governor, Umar Usman Kadafur; Secretary to the State Government, Bukar Tijani; Acting Chief of Staff, Dr. Babagana Mallumbe; and other senior government officials. Members of the NNPCL delegation included the Executive Vice President, Upstream, Mr. Udy Ntia, and the Executive Vice President, Gas, Power and New Energy, Mr. Olalekon Ogunleye. item.title: Five Things To Know Today
item.description: Today’s ‘Five Things’ leads with President Tinubu’s new foreign borrowing request, a six-month transport allowance for federal workers, an updated death toll from the Taraba killings, INEC’s investigation into suspicious photographs in the voters’ register, and the findings of the inquiry into deaths in NSCDC custody. 1. Tinubu seeks approval for $20.5 billion and €1.05 billion in fresh foreign loans President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to approve approximately $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion in external borrowing under the Federal Government’s 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan. The request was presented to the Senate on Tuesday, 27 October. The President says the financing will support infrastructure, power, transport, healthcare, agriculture, education and employment-related projects across the country. Senate President Godswill Akpabio referred the request to the relevant committees, directing them to report within one week. Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has urged lawmakers to withhold approval pending greater disclosure of project details. The borrowing has not yet been approved. Why it matters: The proposed borrowing is substantial and could have long-term implications for Nigeria’s debt obligations, public finances and infrastructure investment. Watch: The Senate committee’s findings, project-by-project disclosures, loan terms and the Debt Management Office’s assessment of repayment obligations. 2. Federal Government approves ₦70,000 monthly transport support for workers A conciliation meeting between the FG and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC). X/@LabourMinNG The Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress reached several agreements during Tuesday’s negotiations in Abuja, easing immediate tensions over threatened industrial action. The government approved a ₦70,000 monthly transport intervention for federal public service workers across all grade levels, beginning in November 2026 and lasting six months. It also agreed to pay outstanding peculiar-allowance arrears in three monthly instalments and settle 19 months of outstanding health workers’ allowances over three months, beginning in December. However, the parties did not reach agreement on the effective date for a revised national minimum wage. They agreed to establish a negotiation committee and review implementation after one month. Why it matters: The intervention could provide temporary relief to federal workers facing high transport and living costs. It is not a permanent wage increase. item.title: Violence Mars Gov Radda’s Funtua Campaign Flag-off As Supporters Report Injuries, Property Losses
item.description: Violence erupted along the route to the Tinubu–Dikko campaign flag-off in Funtua Zone on Wednesday, leaving several supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) injured and their property destroyed. The victims, who said they were travelling in the convoy of Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Radda, alleged that they were attacked by groups of angry youths and hoodlums while heading to the campaign venue, where the Governor was scheduled to present his administration’s Building Your Future scorecard. Some of the affected supporters told reporters that mobile phones, clothing and other personal belongings were destroyed during the incident, while several people sustained varying degrees of injuries. According to the victims, the attackers, whom they described as armed with machetes, knives, stones and bottles, assaulted them without provocation. “We were simply on our way to attend the campaign flag-off when we encountered some angry youths who attacked us with stones and bottles. Many people were injured, and our property was destroyed. We cannot afford to replace what we lost,” one of the victims said. The victims appealed to security agencies and relevant authorities to investigate the incident and bring those responsible to justice. Earlier, at the Malumfashi town roundabout linking Bakori Local Government Area, stones were seen scattered across the road, while several vehicles reportedly had their windscreens damaged, suggesting earlier disturbances in the area. Despite the disruption, Governor Radda proceeded with the presentation of his administration’s Building Your Future scorecard, highlighting achievements recorded since assuming office and outlining ongoing projects across key sectors ahead of the 2027 governorship election. The statewide campaign is designed to deepen grassroots engagement by taking the administration’s performance and development agenda directly to communities across the three senatorial zones of Funtua, Daura and Katsina, covering all 34 Local Government Areas and 361 wards. Authorities had not issued an official statement on the reported attack at the time of filing this report.
